title.rendered: Blessed Are the Peacemakers: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.” A morning devotional on the family resemblance of a Christian.

content.rendered:
In 9 BC, the Emperor Augustus dedicated the Altar of Peace in Rome, a marble monument to a peace enforced by the sword. On a hillside in Galilee, in an occupied province of that same empire, Jesus announced a very different kind of peace, and a very different kind of peacemaker.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, September 3, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Blessed are the peacemakers, For they shall be called sons of God.”
Matthew 5:9 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

In 9 BC, on the northern edge of the ancient Roman Forum, the Emperor Augustus dedicated the Ara Pacis, the Altar of Peace. It was a magnificent marble monument, carved with imperial processions and celebratory friezes, commemorating what the empire called Pax Romana, the peace of Rome. It was a real peace, in the sense that many wars had ended. It was also a peace enforced by the sword of the Roman legion. Any province that questioned it was crushed. Fifty years later, on a hillside in Galilee, an occupied Roman province, a young rabbi stood up to teach and quietly announced a very different kind of peace, and a very different kind of peacemaker.

“Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.” Jesus is continuing the beatitudes of the Sermon on the Mount. Seventh on the list, He names the peacemakers, and He attaches to them one of the highest titles in the entire New Testament. Sons of God. In first-century Jewish thought, to be called a son of someone was to be recognised as sharing their character. The peacemakers, Jesus says, share the character of the Father Himself, because the Father is the ultimate Peacemaker, having reconciled humanity to Himself at the cross of His Son.

The Greek word Jesus uses for “peacemakers” is eirēnopoios. It is a compound word, from eirēnē (peace) and poieō (to make, to build, to construct). The peacemaker in Jesus’ Kingdom is not a person who avoids conflict. Not a person who passively absorbs offence. Not a person who prays for peace from a safe distance. The peacemaker is an active builder of peace where peace has not yet been made. They step into division and do the costly work of reconciliation. They speak truth into misunderstanding. They forgive first. They bear the discomfort of standing in the middle when others are shouting from the ends.

The Passion Translation opens up the beatitude beautifully: “How blessed you are when you make peace! For then you will be recognized as a true child of God” (Matthew 5:9 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Blessed (enjoying enviable happiness, spiritually prosperous—with life-joy and satisfaction in God’s favor and salvation, regardless of their outward conditions) are the makers and maintainers of peace, for they shall be called the sons of God!” (Matthew 5:9 AMPC). Makers and maintainers of peace. Both verbs matter. Making peace where it does not exist. Maintaining peace where it has been fragilely established.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is not an abstract call. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, there is a division in your world today that needs a peacemaker. A tension in your family. A conflict in your workplace. A misunderstanding in your church. A cold silence in a friendship. The Roman way is to enforce a settlement with the sword of your own will and be done with it. The Kingdom way is to step into the division, at cost to yourself, and do the patient, costly, Jesus-shaped work of reconciliation. That kind of peace-making earns you a name in heaven that no earthly title can rival. You will be called a son of God.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You are the ultimate Peacemaker. At the cross You reconciled me to Yourself when I was Your enemy. Today, in the tensions and divisions around me, I choose to walk in Your peacemaking character. I refuse to enforce peace with the sword of my own will. I choose the harder, costlier work of Christlike reconciliation. I step into division. I speak truth in love. I forgive first. I bear the discomfort of standing in the middle. And I trust You to call me what You promised, a son and daughter of God. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am a peacemaker in Christ. I step into division. I do the costly work of reconciliation. I am called a son of God because I share the character of my Father, the ultimate Peacemaker.

Further Reading

  • 2 Corinthians 5:18-19 (NKJV): He has committed to us the word of reconciliation
